summary: The email names none of the five covered stocks; it concerns Brightstream Car Wash Group (BSCW). Whitlock & Rowe Securities is offering one of 12 buy-side seats at a lunch with the BSCW CFO and head of IR on Tuesday, November 3, hosted by its consumer services analyst. The email also includes highlights from a 22-page research report on BSCW.
why_attention: Replying secures a seat for the desk in a small group with BSCW management, which is limited to 12 buy-side seats. The RSVP closes on a stated date. The company is not one of the five covered names.

sections.quote: We would like to invite you and your team to a small investor lunch with the CFO and head of IR of Brightstream Car Wash Group (BSCW)
Please RSVP to me by Friday, October 23.

summary: The email bears on MSFT. Kensington Vale Securities is offering one of three seats on a 40-minute call with a VP of Business Development at a Taiwanese chip packaging and test house (OSAT). The guest says his company was asked to pull in Q1 packaging and test slots for what he believes is Microsoft's Cobalt 200, at about 25-30% above the summer volume. The sender describes this as unconfirmed and as the guest's own read of the supply chain.
why_attention: Attending gives the desk a direct line to someone who sees Cobalt 200 packaging demand first-hand, which the sender says few people do. Only three seats are offered and confirmation closes at noon the day after the email was sent.

sections.quote: His company has been asked to pull in Q1 test and packaging slots for an Arm-based server CPU that he believes is Microsoft's Cobalt 200.
Please let me know by noon tomorrow.
